title: Taste test review of 'Black UFO,' 'Black Curry Meshi,' and 'Black Donbei': We tried out these three products that proclaim 'Indulgence is Justice!'
excerpt: The news blog specialized in Japanese culture, odd news, gadgets and all other funny stuffs. Updated everyday.
content:
Nov 11, 2026 20:05:00

Nissin Foods is releasing three new products in its 'Immoral BLACK' series, timed to coincide with Black Friday. The concept is to 'unleash your 'black desires' and enjoy food to your heart's content.' The three products are ' Nissin Yakisoba BLACK UFO Garlic Mayo Black Squid Ink Sauce Yakisoba ,' ' Nissin BLACK Donbei Pork Fat Soy Sauce Black Udon, ' and ' Nissin BLACK Curry Meshi Rich Cheese, ' and will be available from November 16th, 2026 (Monday). Nissin Foods kindly sent me some of the products in advance, so I tried them out.

'Immoral BLACK' Series: 3 Products (Released November 16) | News Release | Nissin Foods Group

https://www.nissin.com/jp/company/news/13973/

First up is 'Nissin Yakisoba BLACK UFO Garlic Mayo Black Squid Ink Sauce Yakisoba,' a black version of Nissin Yakisoba UFO.

In addition to the squid ink powder, which adds a 'black' element, garlic seasoning is included for a decadent touch.

One serving (97g) contains 445kcal and 3.8g of salt.

The package includes 'liquid sauce' and 'garlic mayonnaise.'

After pouring in the hot water, wait 3 minutes while the liquid sauce is warming up.

The liquid sauce is pitch black.

Mix it well, add the garlic mayonnaise at the end, and it's done. The black yakisoba, reminiscent of squid ink pasta, combined with the garlic aroma of the garlic mayonnaise, gives off a great sense of guilty pleasure, making you think, 'Eating this for lunch might cause some trouble later...' The spiciness of the sliced chili peppers adds a nice kick, and despite the greasy feeling, it disappeared into my stomach in no time. It's a completely different impression from regular yakisoba with sauce, and I felt like I had discovered a new side of UFO.

Next up is Nissin's BLACK Donbei Pork Fat Soy Sauce Black Udon, a black version of Nissin Donbei.

This one also contains garlic seasoning, which enhances the feeling of indulgence. The black color seems to come from caramel coloring or something similar, rather than squid ink.

One serving (94g) contains 377kcal and 4.7g of salt.

Remove the liquid soup from inside.

Add hot water and wait 5 minutes while the liquid soup warms up.

After 5 minutes, the heated liquid soup is added. The black soup, along with the oil, pours in with a gurgling sound.

When mixed, it settled into a 'udon with a slightly dark broth.' While there was a hint of garlic in the aroma, it was diffused throughout the soup, so the feeling of guilt was somewhat diminished. The richness of the pork fat blended well with the slightly burnt, bittersweet flavor of the dark soy sauce base, making it easy to eat. It would have been nice to have some large pieces of fried tofu that could soak up the soup and increase the feeling of guilt.

Lastly, we have 'Nissin BLACK Curry Meshi Rich Cheese'.

The spiciness level is 'medium spicy,' which is in the middle.

In addition to squid ink powder as a black ingredient, it uses multiple types of cheese, including processed cheese, natural cheese, and other cheese products.

One serving (84g) contains 361g of calories. The salt content is 2.1g.

Cooking is as simple as pouring in the specified amount of hot water.

After pouring in hot water and waiting 5 minutes, lift the lid and stir thoroughly for about 30 seconds.

Since the editorial staff member loves spicy food, the spiciness was on the milder side for them. There was hardly any garlic aroma, perhaps because it was lost in the curry and cheese, but the curry, with its well-melted cheese, was flavorful and definitely something I'd like to have again.

Nissin's 'Immoral BLACK' series will be released on Monday, November 16, 2026. Amazon.co.jp is currently taking pre-orders for a 12-pack of UFO instant noodles for 2,859 yen (238 yen per noodle), a 12-pack of Donbei instant noodles for 2,937 yen (245 yen per noodle), and a 6-pack of Curry Meshi instant noodles for 1,763 yen (294 yen per noodle).
